verses.text: Issachar had four sons: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.

Tola's sons were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel. They led the families of Tola and were brave warriors in their generations. In David's time their fighting men numbered twenty-two thousand six hundred.
Uzzi's son was Izrahiah. Izrahiah's sons were Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah. All five were leaders.
The households of their descendants could field thirty-six thousand troops for battle, because they had many wives and sons.
The family records for all the clans of Issachar listed eighty-seven thousand brave warriors in all.
Benjamin had three sons: Bela, Becher, and Jediael.
Bela's five sons were Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri. They were family heads and brave warriors. Their family records listed twenty-two thousand and thirty-four men.
Becher's sons were Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. These were all his sons.
Their family records listed the heads of their households by generation, with twenty thousand two hundred brave warriors.
Jediael's son was Bilhan. Bilhan's sons were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
These were the descendants of Jediael, listed by their family heads. They had seventeen thousand two hundred brave warriors fit to go out to battle.
Shuppim and Huppim were sons of Ir, and Hushim came from Aher.
Naphtali's sons were Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum. They were descendants of Bilhah.
Manasseh's Aramean concubine bore him Asriel. She also bore Machir, the father of Gilead.
Machir took a wife from the family of Huppim and Shuppim, whose sister was named Maacah. The second was named Zelophehad, and Zelophehad had daughters.
Machir's wife Maacah bore a son and named him Peresh. His brother was named Sheresh, and Sheresh's sons were Ulam and Rakem.
Ulam's son was Bedan. These were the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, whose father was Manasseh.
Gilead's sister Hammolecheth gave birth to Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
Shemida's sons were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
Ephraim's family line included Shuthelah and his son Bered, then Tahath, Eleadah, and another Tahath.
It continued through Zabad and his son Shuthelah, and the family also included Ezer and Elead. The men native to Gath killed Ezer and Elead when they went down to take their livestock.
Their father Ephraim mourned for many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
He slept with his wife, and she became pregnant and bore a son. He named him Beriah because trouble had come on his family.
His daughter was Sheerah. She built Lower and Upper Beth Horon and Uzzen Sheerah.
His descendants included Rephah, then Resheph, Telah, and Tahan,
then Ladan, Ammihud, and Elishama,
then Nun and his son Joshua.
Their land and settlements included Bethel and its towns, Naaran to the east, Gezer and its towns to the west, and Shechem and its towns as far as Azzah and its towns.
Along the border of Manasseh they held Beth Shean, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor with their surrounding towns. The descendants of Joseph son of Israel lived in those places.
Asher's sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Their sister was Serah.
Beriah's sons were Heber and Malchiel. Malchiel was the father of Birzaith.
Heber was the father of Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and their sister Shua.
Japhlet's sons were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These were his children.
Shemer's sons were Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.
His brother Helem's sons were Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
Zophah's sons were Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, and Imrah,
as well as Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
Jether's sons were Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
Ulla's sons were Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
These were Asher's descendants. They were heads of households, outstanding warriors, and leading officials. Their family records listed twenty-six thousand men fit for military service.
